implementation: Use the existing explicit-entropy SysRng verification configuration after wallet proof admission; avoid thread-local RNG initialization. Original AIRs and proving configuration are unchanged.
Derive checked allocation-free release x86_64 bounds for configuration, Uni-STARK domain/round construction, transcript, original numeric AIR evaluation, hiding PCS and FRI/MMCS requests.

Derive fixed periodic table construction/retention and actual p3-commit -> p3-matrix interpolation requests, including every parallel fold/reduce accumulator. Sequential column evaluation joins child work before advancing.
Admit the temporary payload peak under 64 MiB separately from the existing 64 MiB caller-owned proof backing ceiling. Neither component ceiling increases physical reservations.
Add a test-only all-thread allocation-request observer with an allocation-free lock-free hook and unwind-safe scope. Explicit serial ignored probes avoid interference with normal parallel tests.

wallet_verifier_scratch.target: release x86_64, pinned Rust 1.96 and dependency sources
wallet_verifier_scratch.fold_reduce_accumulator_count_bound: at most twice the nonempty indexed row count
wallet_verifier_scratch.persistent_formula: configuration + Uni-STARK rounds/domains + transcript + AIR + diagnostic
wallet_verifier_scratch.observations_measure: cumulative allocator-request bytes, not live peak or RSS

limitations: Payload bounds exclude stacks, allocator metadata/slack, OS entropy internals, tracing callbacks, Rayon/runtime control ownership and enclosing worker/coordinator lifetimes. They do not establish complete physical admission or RSS.

All-thread observations accumulate requests across the call and are compared only with cumulative source bounds. They may exceed modeled simultaneous payload peaks; they do not measure or validate those peaks directly.

Sixteen initial behavioral archives and six final scheduling archives each contain 547 sources. Their sole difference is three test ignore attributes, proved by byte comparison; production code and test bodies are identical.

Four fresh CPU wallet proofs and seven CPU registered proofs were exercised, without exporting proof bytes. Four full-size desktop RTX 5080 proofs remain inherited from 9.106; no fresh GPU throughput or GPU proof is claimed.

Debug and non-x86_64 wallet scratch, full allocator/runtime lifetime composition, broader workloads/live caches, nonempty-child full-size merges, paired throughput, 24 hours AND 150 completed roots, multiple GPUs and AMD/Metal remain open.
Shared/job floors stay at 512 MiB/337 MiB. Ordinary incomplete profiles are still rejected; no production activation or physical cap increase is made.
